html:
The Guianas are the region of northeast South America between the Orinoco and the Amazon, today Guyana, Suriname and French Guiana. The map shows the label Guiana here in 1815, a moment when the colonies were changing hands.

During the wars with Revolutionary and Napoleonic France, Britain had seized the Dutch colonies of Essequibo, Demerara, Berbice and Surinam. In the peace of 1814 and 1815 Britain kept the three western colonies, which it joined in 1831 as British Guiana. Surinam went back to the Netherlands as Dutch Guiana. Portugal, which had occupied Cayenne since 1809, returned it to France in 1817 as French Guiana.

All three were sugar colonies built on the Atlantic slave trade, with Maroon communities in the forest and Indigenous peoples such as the Lokono in the interior.
